work_accident.reformulated_text:
A process for gathering information about work accidents and almost work accidents involves several steps and applies to different groups of people, including those in insured gainful employment, kindergarten children, schoolchildren, students, and self-employed individuals.

For individuals in insured gainful employment, a work accident is considered to occur in various circumstances, including when the accident happens at a location, time, and with a cause related to the insured employment, when working from home, on the direct route to or from work, during training sessions, on the way to or from a doctor's visit if it interrupts the direct route to or from work, when taking a child to or from a childcare facility, and when participating in activities of advocacy groups or professional associations.

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, a work accident is considered to occur if the accident happens in a location, at a time, and with a cause related to the school or university education, when participating in a school event, on the direct route to or from school, when performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum, and in certain professional training orientations.

In agricultural or forestry establishments, accidents can be considered work accidents even if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner, providing accommodation for guests, and performing secondary occupations.

Certain accidents outside of professional activity are also considered work accidents, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident, donating blood, and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation.

Employees must immediately inform their employer of any work accident, near accident, serious and immediate risk to safety and health, and any defect discovered in protection systems. The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate if it has not been reported to the emergency services.

Every work accident resulting in a fatality or injury that prevents a person from working for three days must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. Self-employed individuals must report accidents involving themselves or their employees to the accident insurance provider in good time.

Students and schoolchildren must report accidents to the competent directorate, and schools, educational facilities, and universities must report every work accident resulting in physical injury or death to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days.

In cases of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform, and must report fatalities within three days even if the accident has already been reported.

job_application.reformulated_text: The process involves several entities: the job applicant, job applications, companies, and job offers. The job applicant is expected to regularly report the companies to which they have submitted job applications. Based on these reported job applications, new potential job offers are generated and sent to the job applicant. Companies are required to confirm receipt of job applications and provide a rating for the application. A job interview can be arranged through negotiation. If a company wishes to hire the job applicant, the applicant enters a probation phase with that company. After completing the probation phase, both the job applicant and the company can provide ratings for each other. However, the text does not specify what triggers the end of the probation phase or what the criteria are for a successful probation. The company ratings provided by job applicants can only be viewed by other job applicants after a period of 1 year has passed, but the text does not specify whether this applies to all company ratings or only those provided after the 1-year mark. If a job becomes permanent, the process ends for that job, unless the job applicant rated the company C or less, in which case the job applicant continues to receive new job offers but is no longer required to report their job applications. The text does not specify what happens to the job applicant's existing job applications or job offers when they enter the probation phase or when a job becomes permanent.

The process begins with gathering information about potential maternity leave models, which include details on duration in months and how the leave can be split between parents. From this information, a selection of models is presented to the parent, who then chooses a model. After the parent's selection, relevant information is collected. The text does not specify what this relevant information entails or from whom it is collected. Once this information is gathered, notifications are sent to Social Security and the Company in a timely manner, though the text does not specify what constitutes "in time" for these notifications. The process also involves gathering information from companies, but it does not detail what kind of information or how it is used. As the initially planned maternity leave period comes to an end, the parent is given the opportunity to decide about extending their leave. The text does not specify the conditions under which an extension can be granted, nor the process for making this decision, nor how the external parties are notified of any extension decision.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
The process involves several entities, including work accidents, insured individuals, employers, and accident insurance providers. A work accident is considered to occur under various circumstances, including when it happens in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment. The text does not specify whether these circumstances are exhaustive or if other situations can also be considered work accidents.

For insured gainful employment, specific examples of work accidents are given, including accidents that occur while working from home, on the direct route to or from work, during training sessions, and while making use of advocacy groups or professional associations. The text does not specify whether these examples are mutually exclusive or if an accident can be considered a work accident under multiple circumstances.

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, an accident is considered a work accident if it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education. Additional examples of work accidents for this group include accidents that occur during school events, on the direct route to or from school, and while performing practical tasks prescribed as part of the curriculum. The text does not specify whether these examples are exhaustive or if other situations can also be considered work accidents for this group.

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents even if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment. The text does not specify what constitutes "directly while performing the insured employment" or how this is determined.

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation. The text does not specify whether these accidents are subject to the same reporting requirements as work accidents.

The process involves several reporting requirements. Employees must inform their employer immediately of any work accident, incident that would almost have led to an accident, serious and immediate risk to safety and health, and any defect discovered in protection systems. The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services. The text does not specify what constitutes a "serious injury" or how this is determined.

In addition to these reporting requirements, every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. The text does not specify what constitutes "injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days" or how this is determined.

As a self-employed person, accidents involving people they employ and those that involve them must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time. The text does not specify what constitutes "good time" or how this is determined.

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate. Schools, educational facilities, and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate. The text does not specify what constitutes "physically injured" or how this is determined.

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported. The text does not specify what constitutes "in line with the conditions" or how this is determined.
